habitats: The single dyke-dammed spring basin in the low eastern valley
summary: Exactly one landmark tree stands 28–32 m above the low eastern valley's dyke-dammed spring. Its 2–3 m diameter trunk at breast height, broad buttresses and flexible crown support its size. Groundwater sustains dry-season fruit for rondo, reachable foliage feeds coloso and sheltered forks hold alula nests (F18, F19, F21).

links: The rock-spire dyke dams groundwater and sustains the spring.
Reliable water supports a large crown through eastern seasonal drought.
A 2–3 m diameter trunk and spreading structural roots carry its weight.
Buttresses and flexible branches distribute dense-air wind loads.
chains.play: Navigate to the unique crown, locate the spring and climb established root-and-branch routes.
chains.weakness: Water cannot prevent uprooting in failing soil; damaged roots and dead branches create dangerous routes.
observe: Water emerges beside the dyke between spreading roots.
Broad buttresses rise along the massive trunk.
Fine branches flex above a comparatively steady base.

plausibility.summary: Keep exactly one landmark individual, 28–32 m tall with 2–3 m diameter at breast height and substantial buttresses. Place it only at the low eastern spring basin; oxygen does not explain its height.

analogues.mechanism: Buttress-root anchorage supports resistance to overturning; the groundwater subsidy follows F21.

chains.trait: Dry-season fruit at a permanent spring
links: Eastern meadow grasses cure during summer.
Groundwater and stored resources permit seasonal fruit development.
Rondo visits fleshy fruit and transports some seeds.
Seed movement does not create another landmark giant.
chains.play: Collect ripe fallen fruit and read tracks before entering the shaded feeding hub.
chains.weakness: Predictable fruit attracts predators, and damage or reproductive failure can prevent a crop.
observe: Soft scented fruit falls beside straw-coloured meadow.
Rondo carries fruit beyond the crown.
Seeds occur along routes without another giant tree.

plausibility.summary: Groundwater permits rather than guarantees fruiting. Dispersed seeds do not authorize duplicate landmark instances.

analogues.mechanism: Fruit rewards recruit mobile seed carriers; establishment depends on conditions beyond transport.

poison.signal: Green foliage; softness and scent identify ripe fruit.

gameplay.cover: Buttress bays and deep crown shade, including possible predator cover.
gameplay.nest_material: Shed leaves and small fallen twigs.
gameplay.notes: Exactly one fixed spring landmark. Climbing requires reachable holds or mature attached vines; branch failure and falls remain consequential at 1.05 g.

generator.trunk: Exactly one massive trunk, 2–3 m diameter at breast height, with rough bark and buttresses rising 2–4 m along its base.

branching.buttress: Broad radial plates merge into structural roots on stable spring-basin ground.

leaf.type: Leathery broad blade with drip tip

colour.base: Deep green crown and grey-brown bark
overlay_rules: Fruit ripeness uses softness and scent.
Damp illuminated bark may support musgo_faro.

placement.slope: Only the designated low eastern spring-basin landmark beside the groundwater-damming dyke.
placement.wetness: Reliable groundwater with aerated roots above permanent saturation.
placement.soil: Deep stable mineral soil and humus adjoining the dyke.
placement.fog: Valley fog is supplementary; groundwater supplies the tree.
placement.density: Exactly one instance at the authored spring point. The 20–150 m low-valley range is an editorial placement allowance, not a measured canon elevation; snap the individual to the spring-basin terrain elevation.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen with a concentrated dry-season fruit crop, subject to resource and reproductive failure.
generator.wind_response: Fine branches yield under gusts while the massive buttressed base resists overturning; extreme storms can break limbs.

journal.en: The stone holds the water. The water holds this tree. Everything hungry finds its shade.
journal.es: La piedra retiene el agua. El agua sostiene este árbol. Todo lo que tiene hambre encuentra su sombra.
